name.text: Forming a village water committee and selecting dairy cooperative trainees

questiontext.text:
(a) A village water committee is to be formed by selecting \({@pm@}\) men from \({@pa@}\) volunteers and \({@pw@}\) women from \({@pb@}\) volunteers. How many different committees are possible?

Number of committees = [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) A dairy farmers' cooperative has \({@pn2@}\) members. \({@pr2@}\) members will be chosen to attend a training on improved dairy farming. How many different groups of \({@pr2@}\) members can be chosen?

Number of groups = [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

Because the order in which members are selected does not create a different committee or group, use the combination formula:

\(\displaystyle {}_nC_r = \frac{n!}{r!(n - r)!}\)

Part (a): Forming the village water committee
Select the men and the women separately:

  • Selecting \({@pm@}\) men from \({@pa@}\) volunteers:
    \(\displaystyle {}_{{@pa@}}C_{{@pm@}} = \frac{{@pa@}!}{{@pm@}!\,({@pa@} - {@pm@})!} = \frac{{@pa@}!}{{@pm@}!\,{@men_rem@}!} = \frac{{@men_num_factors@} \times {@men_rem@}!}{({@men_den_factors@}) \times {@men_rem@}!} = \frac{{@men_num_factors@}}{{@men_den_factors@}} = \frac{{@men_num_prod@}}{{@men_den_prod@}} = {@pMen@}\)
  • Selecting \({@pw@}\) women from \({@pb@}\) volunteers:
    \(\displaystyle {}_{{@pb@}}C_{{@pw@}} = \frac{{@pb@}!}{{@pw@}!\,({@pb@} - {@pw@})!} = \frac{{@pb@}!}{{@pw@}!\,{@women_rem@}!} = \frac{{@women_num_factors@} \times {@women_rem@}!}{({@women_den_factors@}) \times {@women_rem@}!} = \frac{{@women_num_factors@}}{{@women_den_factors@}} = \frac{{@women_num_prod@}}{{@women_den_prod@}} = {@pWomen@}\)

By the Fundamental Counting Principle, multiply the two independent counts together:

\(\displaystyle \text{Total committees} = {}_{{@pa@}}C_{{@pm@}} \times {}_{{@pb@}}C_{{@pw@}} = {@pMen@} \times {@pWomen@} = {@ta1@}\)

\(\displaystyle \boxed{ \text{Number of committees} = {@ta1@} }\)

Part (b): Selecting \({@pr2@}\) trainees from \({@pn2@}\) cooperative members
Substitute \(n = {@pn2@}\) and \(r = {@pr2@}\), simplify \(({@pn2@} - {@pr2@})! = {@rem2@}!\), and cancel {@rem2@}!:

\(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn2@}}C_{{@pr2@}} = \frac{{@pn2@}!}{{@pr2@}!\,({@pn2@} - {@pr2@})!} = \frac{{@pn2@}!}{{@pr2@}!\,{@rem2@}!} = \frac{{@b_num_factors@} \times {@rem2@}!}{({@b_den_factors@}) \times {@rem2@}!} = \frac{{@b_num_factors@}}{{@b_den_factors@}} = \frac{{@b_num_prod@}}{{@b_den_prod@}} = {@ta2@}\)

\(\displaystyle \boxed{ \text{Number of groups} = {@ta2@} }\)

questiondescription.text:
Applying Combinations in Real-Life Committee and Group Selection

Grade 11 CBE: Solving real-life selection problems using combinations and the Fundamental Counting Principle.

node.description: Check if student added pMen + pWomen instead of multiplying

truefeedback.text: You added \({}_{{@pa@}}C_{{@pm@}} + {}_{{@pb@}}C_{{@pw@}} = {@pMen@} + {@pWomen@} = {@ta1_add@}\). Because both the men and the women are selected together for the same committee, multiply the two counts: \({@pMen@} \times {@pWomen@}\).

node.description: Check if student ignored gender quotas and pooled all volunteers together

truefeedback.text: You computed \({}_{{@pa+pb@}}C_{{@pm+pw@}} = {@ta1_pool@}\) by pooling all volunteers together. The committee must have exactly \({@pm@}\) men from \({@pa@}\) and \({@pw@}\) women from \({@pb@}\), so compute \({}_{{@pa@}}C_{{@pm@}} \times {}_{{@pb@}}C_{{@pw@}}\).

node.description: Check if student used permutations instead of combinations

truefeedback.text: You used permutations \({}_{{@pa@}}P_{{@pm@}} \times {}_{{@pb@}}P_{{@pw@}} = {@ta1_perm@}\). Since committee members have unranked roles, order does not matter: use combinations \({}_{{@pa@}}C_{{@pm@}} \times {}_{{@pb@}}C_{{@pw@}}\).

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Select the men in \({}_{{@pa@}}C_{{@pm@}}\) ways and the women in \({}_{{@pb@}}C_{{@pw@}}\) ways, then multiply the two results together.

node.description: Check exact number of trainee groups
Check if student used permutations nPr instead of combinations nCr

truefeedback.text: You calculated the permutation \(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn2@}}P_{{@pr2@}} = \frac{{@pn2@}!}{{@rem2@}!} = {@ta2_perm@}\). Because the order in which trainees are chosen does not change the group, divide by \({@pr2@}! = {@b_den_prod@}\) using \(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn2@}}C_{{@pr2@}} = \frac{{@pn2@}!}{{@pr2@}!\,{@rem2@}!}\).

node.description: Check if student omitted (n - r)! in the denominator

truefeedback.text: You divided \({@pn2@}!\) by \({@pr2@}!\) alone, forgetting \(({@pn2@} - {@pr2@})! = {@rem2@}!\) in the denominator. Evaluate \(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn2@}}C_{{@pr2@}} = \frac{{@pn2@}!}{{@pr2@}!\,{@rem2@}!}\).

falsefeedback.text: Incorrect. Order does not matter when selecting a group of trainees, so evaluate \(\displaystyle {}_{{@pn2@}}C_{{@pr2@}} = \frac{{@pn2@}!}{{@pr2@}!\,({@pn2@} - {@pr2@})!} = \frac{{@pn2@}!}{{@pr2@}!\,{@rem2@}!}\).
